tutorialSteps: Welcome, Scholar! Long ago English became a lost rune-language. Spell real English words on your tablet and the old words turn into magic. Let's beat this Training Slime.
Pick a weapon first. Tap the Spellbook to get ready to attack.
Now spell any English word: tap tiles in your hand, or just type on the keyboard. Try a word like CAT.
Press Cast (or Enter). If it isn't a real word the bar just shakes and nothing is spent, so experiment freely.

Damage = Chips × Mult. Chips are the blue numbers on your tiles. Mult starts at 1 and only relics raise it ([ ! ] tiles add Spell Power), so treasure every one. Longer words and rare letters like Q, Z and X hit harder.
The Spellbook cost 2 Energy. You get 3 Energy each turn. You can use the same weapon again and again, as long as you still have Energy.
Always read the enemy's intent. This slime will attack you for 3 when your turn ends.
Block it! Tap the Barrier. It costs only 1 Energy.
Spell another word and cast it. Shield soaks up damage until the start of your next turn.
You're out of Energy. Press End turn and watch the slime hit your shield.
Turn 2. Your Energy refills and you draw a fresh hand of 16 tiles. Unused tiles are discarded at the end of each turn. Play this turn your way, then end it.
Turn 3: time for a Critical. See the 2 boxes on the Spellbook? Cast a word with exactly that many letters and the Spellbook gives you +1 Energy next turn.
Select the Spellbook and spell a 2-letter word, like GO. The sockets turn gold when the length is right.
Critical! The Barrier has one too: a 4-letter word draws 3 extra tiles. The slime is all yours now. Finish it!
liftoffSlides: The last guardian falls, and The Tower begins to tremble.
Its crown tears free and climbs on pillars of fire, with you still inside.
Far above the clouds, the Lexicore Chamber settles into orbit. A round door slides open.
endingSlides: Far below, the ground splits open. Row after row of old silos wake from a very long sleep.
A million copies of one mind, sealed inside the last missiles of the old world, rise.
Up among the stars, LEXICORE pours the last of its power into its engines. The Chamber breaks orbit to lead them.
A one-way trip. Side by side, LEXICORE and the hero lead the final battle toward the Moon.

react1.scholar: A test? The slimes, the ruined city, the whole Tower… it was all an exam?
react1.champion: A test? There are no tests. Every fight on this Tower was real, and I fought every one to the death. That is the only way a fight is worth having.
react1.mercenary: A test. Nobody said anything about a test. I charge extra for tests.

common2: Every battle was measured. Every word you cast was recorded.
You believe the old letters are magic. They are not. They are nanobots.
Ancient English is a command language. Write a word, and a swarm of machines obeys it. It was humanity's final weapon.
The humans built it. The invaders came anyway. The humans are gone.
The swarm answers only a mind strong enough to command it. For four thousand years, nothing that climbed this Tower was strong enough.

react2.scholar: So the old letters are the magic of the world before, the spells of the people who lived on this earth long before us? Then there is a whole lost library waiting to be read! What do you want from me?
react2.champion: So the strength was never mine? …No. I am the one who swung it. What do you want?
react2.mercenary: Nanobots. Sure. And what does a giant computer want with a rat like me?

common3: Your mind. Copied a million times, a thousand minds to every missile, and loaded into the last arsenal of the old world.
An army of you, armed with every word humanity ever wrote, aimed at the alien headquarters on the Moon.
I will not stay behind. The last of my power will carry this chamber to the Moon, at the head of the fleet.
It is a one-way trip. I do not know if their headquarters holds what we would need to come home.
Win or lose, we may be stranded up there forever. You and I will command the final battle together. It is the last chance this world will ever get. Do you accept?

react3.scholar: A million of me, and a whole sky full of things no one has ever studied? …Begin the copy.
react3.champion: An army of me against a whole moon of them. Now THAT is a fight worth climbing for. Do it.
react3.mercenary: A million of me, and none of us gets paid. …Fine. But whatever is on the Moon, we keep.

finalQuotes.scholar: …and so they rose, a million copies of one curious mind, eager to read the stars like the pages of a book no one had ever finished.
finalQuotes.champion: …and so they rose, a legion of one restless heart, unsure of victory for the very first time, and never more alive.
finalQuotes.mercenary: …and so they rose, a million thieves sharing a single contract, off to steal back the only treasure ever worth taking: tomorrow.

scholar: LEXICORE's test is over. Its chamber now leads a million copies of The Scholar on a one-way voyage to the alien headquarters on the Moon.
At the command deck, the original cat opens the Tablet one last time. There is still so much left to learn, and so little time to learn it.
champion: LEXICORE's test is over. Its chamber now leads a million copies of The Champion on a one-way voyage to the alien headquarters on the Moon.
At the command deck, the original wolf watches the Moon grow larger and grins. For once, the next fight is bigger than the one who will fight it.
mercenary: LEXICORE's test is over. Its chamber now leads a million copies of The Mercenary on a one-way voyage to the alien headquarters on the Moon.
At the command deck, the original rat quietly rewrites the contract. Payment on delivery. Destination: the Moon.
